evidence: src/infrastructure/app.ts createApp() is the single place that wires repositories, use cases, controllers, asyncHandler and errorMiddleware.
src/infrastructure/error-middleware.ts errorMiddleware is the only place that maps ValidationError/NotFoundError/ConflictError to 400/404/409.

src/infrastructure/in-memory-*-repository.ts classes implement ProjectRepository/TaskRepository/UserRepository with the same Map-backed pattern; filtering lives only in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject.
src/infrastructure/uuid-id-generator.ts UuidIdGenerator implements the domain IdGenerator port.

src/infrastructure/user-controller.ts and project-controller.ts build `{ id, name }` responses inline while task-controller.ts uses toTaskResponse. This is a small inconsistency and not a confirmed bypass.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is a coherent infrastructure/adapter unit. app.ts wires everything together and server.ts starts it. The other files are HTTP adapters (controllers, asyncHandler, errorMiddleware), in-memory repositories implementing the domain repository ports, and a UUID id generator implementing IdGenerator. Mapping domain errors to HTTP status codes happens only in errorMiddleware, and task filtering happens only in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject. Controllers only call use cases and contain no business rules. One small inconsistency: UserController and ProjectController build their responses inline, while TaskController uses toTaskResponse from application/dtos. dtos.ts wasn't in the material, so I can't confirm it offers user or project mappers that are being bypassed. This isn't enough to fail the unit.
